newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's couriers join cry for open U.S. border.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's couriers join cry for open U.S. border.

text.p: Mexico's couriers on Tuesday joined a growing clamor from the rest of the nation's transport industry to fully open trade with the United States, as was initially conceived under the North American Free Trade Agreement.

Despite pledges from the U.S. government that it will open the border to Mexican shippers, aircraft and trucks, deliveries are still restricted to U.S. border sites, where they are prevented from going to more distant destinations.

"U.S. companies that operate in Mexico can pick-up and do pick-up, and can deliver and do deliver, documents and packages from one city to another within Mexican territory," Mexican Association of Messengers and Couriers President Miguel Alessio Robles said at a NAFTA conference on land transport in Mexico City.
"The Mexican companies cannot offer a similar service from one point to another within the United States," he added.
Alessio asked the U.S. government to grant reciprocity, and allow Mexican companies free reign in the United States for deliveries.
